correctness.rationale: The loss is an even sum of four sech translates. Symmetric pairing and exact differentiation give a cubic stationary polynomial in v=cosh(s)^2/p, with a strictly positive prefactor for s>0. Its discriminant has the factor (h-2)(h-1)^4(h+1)^2 T(h) and the physical boundary sign has factor C(h). The shifted C polynomial has exactly one root h>3 by elementary monotonicity; the shifted T polynomial has exactly one positive shifted root by Descartes, bracketed 9<h<10. A rational sign witness at h=10 and continuity put three roots in the physical domain for all h above the upper threshold; no unexamined roots remain. Derivative sign alternation proves counts and threshold shoulders. The standalone program replayed 81 checks, including exact symbolic identities and independent evaluations of the physical derivative. The numerical checks are supplementary to the analytical proof.

value.rationale: The mathematically motivated observable is the actual number of resolved local maxima in a four-pole dielectric loss, not the nominal number of relaxation modes. The complete algebraic two-threshold diagram answers a natural resolution question, exposes a noncentral fold absent in the three-pole model, rules out the seemingly plausible three-peak region, and quantifies the high-separation minima and peak positions. This is a complete continuum classification and not a routine numerical fit. Physical scope is explicitly restricted to an ideal equal-strength uncoupled response.
